sections.html:
The City of Sarasota doesn't mail its own tax bill. A house inside city limits gets a single notice from the county tax collector, with the city listed as one of several taxing bodies. The county appraiser's value is the starting point for every line.

Expect city, county, school board and district charges to share the page with non-ad valorem items for services like fire protection and trash. Start with the appraiser's property search to find your parcel, then open the collector's account page to see what has been billed. For the full county calendar, read the county tax guide. Our selling page for Sarasota covers offers and closing.

The ballot summary raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, then indexes it. It also cuts the yearly cap on non-homestead assessment growth from 10 percent to 5 percent.

New arrivals are treated differently. Anyone who is not a Florida resident on December 31, 2026 gets the current exemption first and the larger one from the fifth year. Local governments would also be limited to listed uses of property tax revenue, including public safety, schools, infrastructure and debt service. The effective date is January 1, 2027.

Locally, the 2026 notice is payable as issued, and the changes reach the 2027 bill. School taxes and non-ad valorem charges stay. If you're pricing a house, ask the appraiser what the changes mean for your parcel.

The appraiser asks for evidence of ownership and of residency, plus details about any earlier home. You must be a Florida resident living in the house on January 1, and March 1 is the timely application date.

A recorded deed, tax bill or TRIM notice shows ownership. For residency, bring a Florida license or ID with the home address, and at least one of voter registration, vehicle registration or a recorded declaration of domicile. A second route uses two items from a different list: a W-2 or paystub, children's school registration, a federal tax return, or utility and bank records. If you still own your old home, show that its exemption was cancelled. If you sold it, show the sale date.

  • Both spouses supply their details.
  • Each applicant needs a Social Security number.
  • A permanent resident who is not a citizen shows a green card.

sections.h2: The Save Our Homes cap at a sale
sections.html:
The cap stops for you at closing. It limits yearly assessed growth to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and a sale lets the appraiser reset the parcel to just value the next January 1.

The state's cap chart, revised in January 2026, shows 3.0 percent for 2024, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 2.7 percent for 2026. A family that has owned a Sarasota home for decades may carry a wide gap between assessed and market value, and the buyer starts without it.

Portability cushions the loss for the seller. Establish a new Florida homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you left the old one, and file DR-501T with the DR-501 by March 1. The transferred amount is the lesser of $500,000 or the old home's just-minus-assessed gap, and 2026 amendments first apply to the 2027 roll.

sections.h2: Exemptions that don't require living there
sections.html:
Four $5,000 exemptions can be claimed on any one Florida property a permanent resident owns: widow or widower, total and permanent disability, blindness, and disabled veteran at 10 percent or higher.

Other benefits need homestead. Seniors of limited means may qualify for an added exemption, with income papers due June 1. A veteran with a total and permanent service-connected disability may have homestead tax waived, and the benefit can pass to a surviving spouse.

You can sell a Sarasota house that has back taxes. The balance is cleared through closing. Tax left unpaid after April 1 turns delinquent, and the collector warns that it can eventually cost the owner the property.

The buyer answers to the collector for the entire bill, whenever the purchase happens. Your share appears on the settlement statement as a credit, not as a payment to the collector. A bill that reaches a former owner goes back to the new owner or to the collector. At the clerk's counter, the deed carries stamp tax of $0.70 per $100, rounded up. A long delinquency can lead to the process on our tax deed page.

Practical order of steps: request the balance, give it to the title agent, review the payoff on the closing statement, and keep the receipt.

sections.h2: Paperwork for disability and widow exemptions
sections.html:
Each claim has its own proof. Gather it before March 1 so a first-time filing isn't held up.

  • Widow or widower: an application, and possibly a copy of the death certificate. Remarriage ends the exemption.
  • Total and permanent disability: a Florida physician's certification on form DR-416, or a certificate from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs.
  • Blindness: a certificate from the state Division of Blind Services, the VA or the Social Security Administration, or a physician or optometrist form.
  • Disabled veteran: a letter, certificate or ID card from the government showing the rating.
  • Wheelchair or legally blind homestead exemption: two unrelated Florida physicians on DR-416, plus a Statement of Gross Income on DR-501A.

The income test for that last exemption counts VA benefits and Social Security.

Value goes first to the appraiser and then to the Value Adjustment Board, within 25 days of the TRIM mailing. Rates go to the budget hearings listed on the notice.

The board decides value, classification and exemption questions only. Florida's calendar puts tentative budget hearings in September and October and final hearings after that.

sections.h2: Handling a tax problem in order
sections.html:
Match each question to the office that owns it: value and exemptions to the appraiser, the bill to the collector, recorded paper to the clerk.

  • Open your parcel on the appraiser's search and view the TRIM through the button near the top of the record.
  • Check that exemptions survived any name or address change.
  • Look for a prior-year balance on the collector's account page.
  • Search the clerk's Official Records for liens.
  • Join the clerk's fraud alerts for the owner's name.

Work through the list before you list the house. A buyer's title search will find any open item anyway, so it's cheaper to learn about it first.

faqs.q: Does the City of Sarasota collect property tax itself?
faqs.a: No. The county tax collector bills for every taxing body inside the city, so you pay one notice.

faqs.q: What is the city millage rate?
faqs.a: The city sets its own rate, which is one line on your bill. Read your TRIM notice or ask the city or appraiser for the current figure.

faqs.q: When must I apply for homestead?
faqs.a: By March 1, having lived in the house as your permanent home on January 1. Late filings are still reviewed.

faqs.q: Does the Save Our Homes cap pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets assessed value to just value the next January 1, though portability may carry part of the benefit to your next Florida home.

faqs.q: Can I sell with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, and the balance is normally settled from the proceeds at closing after the title agent confirms the amount.
